title: Maximum-cardinality matching

problem.name: Maximum-cardinality matching
problem.statement_latex:
Output $M\subseteq E$ maximizing $|M|$, subject to every vertex occurring in at most one edge of $M$. The input may be bipartite or general. Matching models assignment and resource allocation.
The comparison uses quantum time with coherent adjacency-array access and classical RAM or field-arithmetic time on explicit graphs.
problem.statement_text: Output $M\subseteq E$ maximizing $|M|$, subject to every vertex occurring in at most one edge of $M$. The input may be bipartite or general. Matching models assignment and resource allocation. The comparison uses quantum time with coherent adjacency-array access and classical RAM or field-arithmetic time on explicit graphs.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(n\sqrt{m+n})$ for bipartite graphs; $\widetilde O(n^{3/2}\sqrt m+n^2)$ for general graphs, Ambainis--\v Spalek.
quantum.details_latex: The matching is stored classically, and quantum access supports augmenting-path and blossom operations. These are time upper bounds for explicit classical output under coherent adjacency access.
quantum.headline_text: $\widetilde O(n\sqrt{m+n})$ for bipartite graphs; $\widetilde O(n^{3/2}\sqrt m+n^2)$ for general graphs, Ambainis–Špalek.
quantum.details_text: The matching is stored classically, and quantum access supports augmenting-path and blossom operations. These are time upper bounds for explicit classical output under coherent adjacency access.

classical.headline_latex: $m^{1+o(1)}$ for bipartite graphs, almost-linear maximum flow; $\min\{O(m\sqrt n),O(n^{9/4+\varepsilon})\}$ for general graphs.
classical.details_latex: Bipartite cardinality matching reduces to unit-capacity flow. For general graphs, Micali--Vazirani supplies the sparse combinatorial bound and randomized algebraic matching uses $O(n^\omega)$ field operations. The bound $\omega\le9/4$ yields the displayed algebraic time for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. The minimum of these classical bounds is asymptotically at least as strong as the stated quantum bounds.

strength.description_latex: The displayed quantum algorithms have no current worst-case time advantage over these classical algorithms.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant coherent adjacency access is needed. Search registers are logarithmic in $n$, while matching, blossom and layered-graph records require polynomial classical storage with reversible query support.
